cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-woven, indigo-dyed strip-cloth boubou gown with hand embroidery, a well-known traditional West African men's garment style associated with Wolof and neighboring Senegambian groups; nothing contradicts the Wolof attribution.

physical.title: gown
physical.summary: Man’s gown (boubou, tobe), hand-woven from hand-spun cotton dyed in indigo. The body is formed of wide strips hand-sewn together along the selvedges vertically, while the sleeves are sewn horizontally. At the front has been sewn a large pocket. Both the front and the back are extensively embroidered with hand-sewn decoration in white, yellow, green and red imported European cotton thread using some buttonhole eyelet stitching. These form geometrical patterns with a large spiral, and zig-zags, outlined bands and circles. Small holes sewn around the edges with buttonhole stitch in yellow silk thread occur throughout. The back of the gown is embroidered with similar patterns using same colour threads, and there is a second spiral at the back of neck.
